S1.title: Ml Project Handbook
S1.text:
Project Deliverables and Compute Policy
Every project delivers a model card, two baselines and an error analysis. Training must finish in under 30 minutes on a laptop CPU. Allowed libraries are scikit-learn, pandas, numpy and matplotlib.

S2.title: Ml Model Evaluation Runs
S2.text: Dataset ml_model_evaluation_runs: 10 rows, columns: run_id, model, task, train_accuracy, val_accuracy, precision, recall, f1, notes.

S3.title: Ml Reference Notes
S3.text: Feature: an input variable used by a model, for example a person's age. Label or target: the value the model should predict. Hyperparameter: a setting chosen before training, such as the learning rate, tree depth or number of neighbors k. Parameter: a value learned during training, such as the weights of linear regression. Epoch: one full pass through the training data. Batch size: the number of examples used for one gradient update. Learning rate: the step size of gradient descent. Regularization: a penalty that discourages overly complex models. L2 (ridge) shrinks weights; L1 (lasso) can set weights to zero. Overfitting: low training error but high validation error because the model memorized noise. Underfitting: high error on both training and validation data because the model is too simple. Bias: error from wrong or overly simple assumptions.

S5.title: Ml Lecture Notes
S5.text: is bias squared plus variance plus irreducible noise. Increasing model complexity lowers bias but raises variance.  Ways to reduce overfitting include collecting more training data, simplifying the model, regularization (L1 and L2 penalties that shrink weights; L1 can drive weights to exactly zero), early stopping, dropout for neural networks, feature selection and cross-validation to choose hyperparameters. Learning curves, which plot error against training set size, help diagnose whether a model suffers from high bias or high variance.
